title: Impact of Financial Product Marketing Tactics on Less Financially Literate Consumers
what_it_is: Impact of Financial Product Marketing Tactics on Less Financially Literate Consumers

sections.label: MAS proposed roadshow measures
sections.summary: MAS proposed measures requiring financial institutions to disclose identities, monitor representatives, conduct call-backs and surveys, offer more time, limit gifts, and hold roadshows in commercial premises.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: For example, one, representatives of FIs must disclose their identities upfront and clearly to prospective clients; two, FIs should monitor the conduct of their representatives at roadshows through site visits and mystery shopping; three, FIs should conduct call-backs and surveys within the free-look period to check if clients understood the products that they purchased at roadshows.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: MAS has also proposed additional new measures, such as requiring FIs to: one, offer consumers additional time of at least three to five days to consider their decisions; two, limit the use of gifts to influence consumers’ decision-making; and three, conduct roadshows and marketing events only in commercial premises instead of public spaces, such as streets and pedestrian areas.

sections.label: Call-back for vulnerable clients
sections.summary: A supervisor from the financial institution must call the client to check understanding of the product and risks before any sale to vulnerable clients is completed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: A supervisor from the FI must call the client to check back on his or her understanding of the product and risks before any sale to vulnerable clients is allowed to be completed.

sections.label: FIDReC adjudication binding on FIs
sections.summary: FIDReC's adjudication outcome binds financial institutions but not consumers, who retain the right to pursue claims through other avenues such as legal advice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The outcome of FIDReC's adjudication is binding on the FIs, but not on consumers, who retain the right to pursue their claims through other avenues, such as seeking legal advice on the merits of their case.

sections.label: Question on retroactive compensation
sections.summary: A Member asked whether MAS would require retroactive compensation to consumers if a financial institution breached a threshold of aggressive or inappropriate marketing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, maybe the Minister of State can help me clarify that point.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I appreciate that MAS performs a regulatory check and balance on the FIs, but it does not sound to me like the individuals who fall prey to such marketing techniques have any form of recourse or compensation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, my question is: should MAS find any particular FI in breach of a certain threshold of aggressive or inappropriate marketing, will there be retroactive forms of compensations required of them to be made to the consumer?

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: As I mentioned earlier on, MAS will review reports of breaches of misconduct and take appropriate regulatory actions against FIs or representatives that are found to breach MAS regulations.
